method: Exported all 44 slides that contain pending objects from the read-only original PPTX with local PowerPoint at 1600x900. For the first ten such slides, compared each candidate crop with its full rendered original. Unsupported OLE objects without a crop were located by native slide shape path, ID and bounds before judging the visible drawing. Decisions below are local proposals, not product review writes.

objects.reason: Photo of black and white POF ends illustrates the surrounding native material description; no separately readable specification or measurement.

objects.evidenceText: The SI-POF cross-section drawing distinguishes radiation, higher, lower and cladding modes and shows rays taking different paths through the fiber. The slide marks an area of higher attenuation and relates ray angle to mode behavior.
objects.reason: The embedded OLE object's native shape path 1, shape ID 20, bounds 0.59/1.68/5.39/2.77 inches, maps to the upper-left diagram in the original slide. It is explanatory, not a measured modal profile.

The rendered equation visibly contains attenuation, relative mode delay and mode-mixing terms, but OCR omits mathematical operators and the exact derivative grouping is not yet verified against the embedded source. Do not index a guessed formula.

The full slide contains a wavelength-versus-attenuation curve and colored windows, while the transparent candidate crop drops axes and labels. Unit glyphs and curve provenance need a reliable transcription before publication; the graph is substantive, not decoration.

objects.evidenceText: The left mode-mixing schematic depicts a ray encountering a labeled scattering center inside the fiber and changing direction.
objects.reason: Embedded OLE shape path 7, shape ID 11, bounds 0.75/2.72/4.48/1.25 inches, maps to the upper-left drawing; the original slide provides the label.

objects.evidenceText: The right mode-mixing schematic labels core, cladding and a scattering center near an irregular boundary, with outgoing rays diverging after the interaction.
objects.reason: Embedded OLE shape path 8, shape ID 12, bounds 4.43/3.97/4.94/1.58 inches, maps to the lower-right drawing; it illustrates the slide's claim rather than quantifying a rate.

objects.evidenceText: The bending diagram labels launched light rays, bend radius, rays guided only by cladding and rays guided by cladding behind the bend. It depicts different ray paths through and beyond a bend.
objects.reason: Embedded OLE shape path 4, shape ID 8, bounds 0.75/1.10/8.35/6.04 inches, covers the visible diagram; no attenuation number is inferred from it.

The chart has two series, four bending radii and decimal-comma data labels, but its attenuation unit is not sufficiently clear in the render. It contains material measured values and cannot be discarded or published with an uncertain unit.
White/transparent overlaid picture at the same LED photo area carries no visible independent content in the original rendering.
LED package photograph illustrates the separately extracted LED-light-source bullets; it does not establish a component model or additional numeric rating.
White/transparent overlaid picture in the photodiode photo area has no visible independent content.
White/transparent overlaid picture in the die photo area has no visible independent content.
Receiver-package photograph illustrates the separately extracted Si-PIN photodiode text; no component model or measured result is shown.
Photodiode die photograph illustrates the receiver description; no separate dimensions or performance values are legible.

objects.evidenceText: The PD responsivity graph plots responsivity in A/W against wavelength in nm. The shown curve peaks at about 0.53 A/W near 700 nm and declines toward longer wavelengths; green and red wavelength bands are highlighted without a legend.
objects.reason: The candidate crop is transparent and omits axes; the full original slide supplies axes and approximate curve position. Values are approximate readings of this historical slide, not device guarantees.
Connector photograph illustrates the native in-line connector caption and attenuation bullet; its appearance does not establish the 1.0–2.5 dB figure.
Exploded connector photograph is an illustration; dimensions and performance are not independently specified by the image.

remaining: Continue original-slide comparison for the remaining 112 objects; resolve the three substantive formula/chart objects through reliable source data or retain them unresolved. Complete product review and then isolated tree reading and exact citation checks for slides 5 and 22.
